family_title: LoRA and its training-dynamics / scaling variants

methods.name: LoRA
methods.full_name: Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0 x + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A x,\qquad W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A,\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B)\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer; the paper adapts W_q and W_v of Transformer attention (PEFT also supports target_modules='all-linear', embeddings, conv)
methods.structure: \Delta W = \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA factors through an r-dimensional space, i.e. it is the image of the multiplication map \mu:\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\times\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\to\{\mathrm{rank}\le r\}; the factorization is only defined up to the gauge action (B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A),\ R\in GL(r).
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 + (alpha/r) B A can be computed once and stored in place of W_0, so inference runs the original architecture with no extra latency (and can be unmerged by subtraction).
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (A random Gaussian in the paper; Kaiming-uniform in HF PEFT), so Delta W = 0 and the model starts exactly at the pretrained function; alpha/r rescaling is fixed (alpha set to the first r tried and not tuned).
methods.key_idea: Freeze the pretrained weights and learn the weight update as a product of two thin matrices, exploiting the hypothesis that task-adaptation updates have low intrinsic rank; because the update is linear in W it can be merged away after training.
methods.results_note: On GPT-3 175B LoRA reduces trainable parameters ~10,000x and training GPU memory ~3x while matching or exceeding full fine-tuning on WikiSQL, MNLI and SAMSum; it is on par with full fine-tuning on RoBERTa/DeBERTa (GLUE) and GPT-2 (E2E).

relations.note: LoRA was motivated as an adapter alternative without serial inference latency
compared as a baseline in the LoRA paper

methods.name: rsLoRA
methods.full_name: Rank-Stabilized LoRA
methods.paper_title: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma_r\, B A,\qquad \gamma_r = \tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r}}\ \ (\text{instead of LoRA's } \tfrac{\alpha}{r});\quad W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B)\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: same as LoRA (paper adapts all attention and MLP linear layers of Llama 2)
methods.structure: Identical rank-r factorization \Delta W=\gamma_r BA; only the scalar multiplier changes. Theorem: with B=0 and A i.i.d. with r-independent variance, adapters are rank-stabilized (forward outputs and backward gradients \Theta_r(1) as r\to\infty) iff \gamma_r\in\Theta(1/\sqrt{r}).
methods.mergeable_reason: Only a scalar on the LoRA branch changes, so W_0 + gamma_r B A merges exactly like LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (standard LoRA initialization), so Delta W = 0; the paper notes that rank-correcting only the initialization instead of the multiplier is unstable at large rank.
methods.key_idea: LoRA's alpha/r multiplier is overly aggressive: it makes gradients collapse as rank grows, so higher ranks learn no better than rank 4-8; dividing by sqrt(r) instead keeps learning rank-stable and lets extra rank buy extra performance at no inference cost.
methods.results_note: Fine-tuning Llama 2 on 20k OpenOrca examples with ranks 4 to 2048, rsLoRA's fine-tuning perplexity keeps improving with rank whereas standard LoRA plateaus and shows collapsing gradient norms at high rank.

relations.note: changes only the rank-dependent scale gamma_r
LoRA Without Regret argues 1/r makes the optimal LR roughly rank-independent (early training), whereas rsLoRA argues 1/sqrt(r) is needed for large-rank stability
both are width/rank-scaling (muP-style) corrections of LoRA hyperparameters

methods.name: LoRA+
methods.full_name: LoRA+ (decoupled learning rates for A and B)
methods.paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA;\qquad A \leftarrow A - \eta_A\, g_A,\quad B \leftarrow B - \eta_B\, g_B,\quad \eta_B = \lambda\,\eta_A,\ \ \lambda\gg 1\ (\text{e.g. } \lambda=2^4)
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Unchanged rank-r factorization; the optimizer applies a block-diagonal learning-rate operator \mathrm{diag}(\eta_A I,\ \lambda\eta_A I) to (A,B). Infinite-width analysis: efficient feature learning requires \eta_A=\Theta(n^{-1}),\ \eta_B=\Theta(1), i.e. \eta_B/\eta_A=\Theta(n) (n = model width); this explicitly breaks the GL(r) gauge symmetry in favour of B.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the training procedure changes; the trained adapter is a standard LoRA product that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard B = 0 with A random of variance Theta(1/n) (Init[1]); the paper also analyses the reverse A = 0, B random (Init[2]). Delta W = 0 in both cases.
methods.key_idea: With one shared learning rate, A and B cannot both learn features efficiently as width grows; setting the B learning rate a fixed large multiple of the A learning rate fixes this while keeping a 1-D LR search.
methods.results_note: Reports 1-2% accuracy improvements and up to ~2x faster fine-tuning at the same compute as LoRA (RoBERTa/GPT-2 on GLUE, Llama-7b on MNLI and MMLU); best ratio is task/model dependent (~2^4 for RoBERTa with Init[2], ~2^1-2^2 for Llama).

relations.note: same parametrization, different per-factor learning rates
both fix the A/B learning-rate imbalance; LoRA+ with a fixed scalar ratio, Riemannian LoRA with an r x r preconditioner and a single learning rate
the eta_A -> 0 limit of LoRA+ freezes A and trains only B

methods.name: LoRA-FA
methods.full_name: LoRA with Frozen-A (and projected B-gradient)
methods.paper_title: LoRA-FA: Memory-efficient Low-rank Adaptation for Large Language Models Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,B A_0,\ \ s=\tfrac{\alpha}{r};\quad A_0\ \text{random and frozen},\ B\ \text{trained with}\ \ \tilde g_B = \tfrac{1}{s^{2}}\,\nabla_B\mathcal{L}\,(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}\ \Rightarrow\ s\,\tilde g_B A_0 = G\,A_0^{\top}(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}A_0,\ \ G=\nabla_W\mathcal{L}
methods.locus: same as LoRA (any linear layer)
methods.structure: \Delta W = sBA_0 with A_0 a fixed random r\times d_{in} matrix, so updates live in the linear space \mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\otimes\mathrm{row}(A_0); the corrected gradient makes each induced weight step the orthogonal projection G P_{A_0} (P_{A_0}=A_0^{\top}(A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1}A_0) of the full gradient onto that fixed subspace.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter is still an additive rank-r product B A_0 that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 with A_0 random (Gaussian or uniform; the paper ablates the choice) and never updated, so Delta W = 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Freezing the down-projection A means backprop only needs the r-dimensional activation XA instead of the full input X, making activation memory insensitive to rank; the current version additionally rescales B's gradient by (AA^T)^{-1} so the induced update is the best Frobenius approximation of the full gradient within the frozen row space (the 2023 v1 only froze A).
methods.results_note: The current version reports performance competitive with full fine-tuning and LoRA variants on GLUE (RoBERTa) and on GSM8K/HumanEval/MT-Bench after SFT of Llama-2/Llama-3/Qwen3/DeepSeek-V2-Lite, with substantially reduced activation memory.

relations.note: LoRA with eta_A = 0
LoRA-Pro's gradient-matching objective with g^A constrained to 0 yields exactly LoRA-FA's corrected B-gradient
with A frozen the correction equals the Riemannian B-preconditioner (AA^T)^{-1} up to the constant s^{-2}
same freeze-A/train-B asymmetry; AsyLoRA supplies the generalization theory, LoRA-FA the memory argument and gradient projection

methods.name: Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA
methods.full_name: Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA (scaled GD / scaled AdamW)
methods.paper_title: Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+BA:\quad A \leftarrow A - \eta\,(B^{\top}B+\delta I_r)^{-1}\nabla_A\mathcal{L},\qquad B \leftarrow B - \eta\,\nabla_B\mathcal{L}\,(AA^{\top}+\delta I_r)^{-1};\quad \text{to first order } \delta W \approx -\eta\,(P_B G + G P_A)
methods.locus: same as LoRA (PEFT preconditions nn.Linear-shaped lora_A/lora_B only)
methods.structure: r\times r preconditioners from the Mishra et al. Riemannian metric on the quotient manifold (\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}_*\times\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}_*)/GL(r) of rank-r matrices; the induced step P_BG+GP_A (P_B=B(B^{\top}B)^{-1}B^{\top},\ P_A=A^{\top}(AA^{\top})^{-1}A) depends only on BA, so plain scaled GD is invariant to the gauge (B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A).
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the optimizer changes; the trained adapter is a standard LoRA product.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA init (B = 0); because B^T B is singular at init a damping delta*I (reg in PEFT) is added before inversion.
methods.key_idea: Precondition each factor's gradient by the inverse Gram matrix of the other factor, turning LoRA's update into (approximately) the projection of the full gradient onto col(B) and row(A); under infinite width this yields stable feature learning with a single learning rate for A and B, at negligible r x r cost.
methods.results_note: Scaled GD closes the SGD-AdamW gap and scaled AdamW improves AdamW for GPT-2 LoRA fine-tuning on E2E NLG, and the preconditioner makes Stable Diffusion / Mix-of-Show LoRA fine-tuning markedly more robust to the learning rate, with runtime close to unscaled optimizers.

relations.note: optimizer-only change
solves the same A/B learning-rate imbalance with a matrix preconditioner instead of a scalar ratio

methods.name: LoRA-RITE
methods.full_name: Robust Invariant Transformation Equilibration for LoRA
methods.paper_title: LoRA Done RITE: Robust Invariant Transformation Equilibration for LoRA Optimization
methods.formula_latex:

methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Adaptive one-sided r\times r matrix preconditioning of 'unmagnified' gradients expressed in orthonormal bases of the factors; moments are transported between successive bases and an 'escaped mass' \rho I compensates lost second-moment mass. The resulting W-update is exactly invariant under (B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A),\ R\in GL(r) (transformation invariance).
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the optimizer changes; the adapter remains a mergeable LoRA product.

methods.results_note: Replacing Adam with LoRA-RITE for LoRA tuning of Gemma-2B gives +4.6% accuracy on Super-Natural Instructions and +3.5% averaged over HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K and OpenBookQA; with Gemma-7B-IT it reaches 55.50% on GSM8K vs 48.37% for Adam.

relations.note: Riemannian GD is transformation invariant but ScaledAdam (with element-wise Adam) is not; RITE restores invariance with adaptivity
both address one factor dominating optimization
optimizer-only change

methods.name: LoRA-Pro
methods.full_name: LoRA-Pro (equivalent-gradient matching)
methods.paper_title: LoRA-Pro: Are Low-Rank Adapters Properly Optimized?
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Gradient surgery on the fixed-rank manifold: the 'equivalent gradient' becomes \tilde g = P_BG+(I-P_B)GP_A, the orthogonal projection of the full gradient G onto the tangent space of rank-r matrices at BA (closed-form minimiser of \|\tilde g-G\|_F); the residual r\times r gauge freedom X is fixed by a Sylvester equation keeping (g^A,g^B) closest to the vanilla LoRA gradients. The AdamW variant keeps moments of the full-size equivalent gradient.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the optimizer changes; the result is a standard LoRA adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA init (B = 0); the closed form assumes full-rank B and A, so inverses must be regularized while B is rank-deficient early in training.
methods.key_idea: Training LoRA is equivalent to full fine-tuning with a low-rank 'equivalent gradient' sBg^A + sg^BA; choosing g^A, g^B to make this as close as possible to the true full gradient (closed form, guaranteed loss decrease) narrows the gap to full fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: On a GLUE subset with T5-base LoRA-Pro beats standard LoRA by 6.36 points on average (above full fine-tuning), and on Llama-2-7B it beats LoRA-GA by 2.85 (GSM8K) and 6.45 (HumanEval) at rank 32, at ~4 GB more GPU memory than LoRA.

relations.note: scaled GD gives P_BG+GP_A (double-counting P_BGP_A); LoRA-Pro gives the exact tangent-space projection P_BG+(I-P_B)GP_A
both align LoRA with full fine-tuning gradients: LoRA-GA only at initialization, LoRA-Pro at every step
both approximate full-gradient training with low-rank projected updates

methods.name: ReLoRA
methods.full_name: Restarted LoRA (high-rank training through low-rank updates)
methods.paper_title: ReLoRA: High-Rank Training Through Low-Rank Updates
methods.formula_latex: W^{(k)} = W^{(k-1)} + s\,B_kA_k\ \ (\text{merge every } T \text{ steps}),\qquad \Delta W_{\text{total}}=\sum_{k=1}^{N} s\,B_kA_k,\ \ \mathrm{rank}\le Nr;\quad \text{after each merge: } B_k\leftarrow 0,\ A_k\ \text{re-init},\ \text{prune most Adam moments, LR re-warm-up}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{at any time (after a short full-rank warm start when training from scratch)}
methods.locus: attention and MLP linear layers of Transformer LMs during (pre-)training
methods.structure: Sum of N rank-r increments accumulated by periodic merge-and-reinit: the total update lies in M_{\le r}+\cdots+M_{\le r}=M_{\le Nr} while each phase optimizes only a rank-r chart; uses a jagged cosine schedule and magnitude-pruned (~99%) optimizer state at each restart.
methods.mergeable_reason: LoRA factors are merged into the dense weights at every restart and at the end, leaving a plain dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Each restart re-initializes B = 0 (A Kaiming) so merge-and-reinit leaves the function unchanged; from-scratch training needs a full-rank warm start (e.g. 5k steps) before switching to ReLoRA.
methods.key_idea: Since rank(X+Y) can exceed rank(X), repeatedly merging low-rank updates into the weights and restarting the adapter yields a high-rank total update with low-rank memory; partial optimizer reset and LR re-warm-up stop the new adapter from relearning the old subspace.
methods.results_note: Pre-training Transformer LMs up to 1.3B parameters on C4, ReLoRA performs comparably to full-rank training while saving up to 5.5 GB RAM per GPU and speeding up training by 9-40% depending on model size and hardware.

relations.note: LoRA plus periodic merge-and-restart
both target memory-efficient high-rank (pre-)training via low-rank updates

methods.name: Delta-LoRA
methods.full_name: Delta-LoRA (propagating the low-rank delta into the pretrained weight)
methods.paper_title: Delta-LoRA: Fine-Tuning High-Rank Parameters with the Delta of Low-Rank Matrices
methods.formula_latex: h = W^{(t)}x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B^{(t)}A^{(t)}x;\quad (A,B)\ \text{updated by AdamW};\quad W^{(t+1)} = W^{(t)} + \lambda\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\big(B^{(t+1)}A^{(t+1)}-B^{(t)}A^{(t)}\big)\ \ \text{for } t\ge K;\ \ \text{no dropout on the LoRA branch}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{with optimizer state; all } d_{out}d_{in} \text{ entries of } W \text{ are also modified (no gradient or moments stored for } W)
methods.locus: same as LoRA (paper: GPT-2, BART, RoBERTa weight matrices)
methods.structure: Every step after K adds \lambda times the increment of the rank-r product (itself of rank \le 2r) to the base weight, so W accumulates an unbounded-rank sum of low-rank increments; the increment acts as a surrogate for -\eta\,\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial W, which is exact only without dropout in the branch.
methods.mergeable_reason: The final model is the dense weight W^(T) + (alpha/r) B A, but the pretrained weight itself is overwritten, so the adaptation cannot be stored or swapped as a small detachable adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 and W-updates only start after K steps, so training starts from the pretrained function.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the change of the low-rank product between consecutive steps as a free (no gradient, no optimizer state) update to the full pretrained weight, giving high-rank adaptation at LoRA's memory cost.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA, DyLoRA and AdaLoRA in the paper's experiments on E2E and WebNLG (GPT-2 medium), XSum (BART-large) and GLUE (RoBERTa-base).

relations.note: LoRA branch plus a delta-driven update of W
both push high-rank updates into W; Delta-LoRA does it continuously every step rather than by periodic merges

methods.name: COLA
methods.full_name: Chain of LoRA
methods.paper_title: Chain of LoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models via Residual Learning
methods.formula_latex: W^{(i)} = W_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{i} B_jA_j,\qquad (B_i,A_i) \approx \arg\min_{B_i,A_i}\ \mathcal{L}\big(W^{(i-1)} + B_iA_i\big);\quad \text{then merge ('tie a knot'), re-init } B_{i+1}=0,\ A_{i+1}\sim\mathcal{N},\ \text{reset optimizer}
methods.trainable_params: r_i(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{for the active link (ranks may decrease along the chain)}
methods.locus: same as LoRA (OPT-1.3B, Llama-2-7B)
methods.structure: Residual learning: a chain of M rank-r_i corrections, each fitted to the residual \Delta W^\star-\sum_{j<i}B_jA_j on top of the merged weights; analysed as a (stochastic, non-convex) Frank-Wolfe / conditional-gradient method over low-rank atoms.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each link is merged into the frozen weights as training proceeds, so the final model is a dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Each new link starts with B = 0 and Gaussian A, so extending the chain does not change the function.
methods.key_idea: Approximate the optimal high-rank update by a Frank-Wolfe-like sequence of low-rank residual fits (tune LoRA, merge, extend the chain with a fresh LoRA and reset optimizer state), at LoRA's compute and memory.
methods.results_note: Across OPT-1.3B and Llama-2-7B on seven tasks COLA consistently beats LoRA, e.g. a 6.47% relative test-accuracy gain on WSC with OPT-1.3B and up to 4.4% relative gain with Llama-2-7B.

relations.note: same merge-and-reinit idea applied to fine-tuning, with full optimizer reset and a Frank-Wolfe convergence analysis
same periodic-merge mechanism
chain of standard LoRA modules

methods.name: PeriodicLoRA
methods.full_name: PeriodicLoRA (PLoRA)
methods.paper_title: PeriodicLoRA: Breaking the Low-Rank Bottleneck in LoRA Optimization
methods.formula_latex: W_t = W_{t-1} + s\,B_tA_t\ \ (\text{unload at the end of stage } t),\qquad W_T = W_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T} s\,B_tA_t,\ \ \mathrm{rank}\le Tr;\quad \text{momentum unloading: merge } (1-m)\,sB_tA_t \text{ and keep } (B_t,A_t) \text{ scaled by } m
methods.locus: all attention and MLP linear layers (LLaMA-7B experiments)
methods.structure: Periodic merge-and-reinit (stage length = a fixed number of mini-batches, e.g. ~4.8k examples) accumulating a sum of rank-r terms, with an exponential-moving-average-like 'momentum' that only partially unloads the adapter to stabilize training.
methods.mergeable_reason: Adapters are unloaded into the backbone during training; the final model is dense with the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Each stage re-initializes B = 0, A Gaussian (when m = 0), together with optimizer and LR-scheduler state.
methods.key_idea: Unload LoRA weights into the backbone after every few hundred steps and restart them, so multiple low-rank updates accumulate into a higher-rank update at constant memory; a momentum-based partial unload prevents collapse across mini-batches.
methods.results_note: With LLaMA-7B instruction tuning PLoRA consistently outperforms LoRA at the same rank (reporting up to ~1.8x LoRA's 'learning ability') without extra memory.

relations.note: same merge-and-restart idea for fine-tuning; PLoRA adds momentum unloading
concurrent periodic-merge method
periodically restarted LoRA

methods.name: LoRA Dropout
methods.full_name: LoRA Dropout (sparsity-regularizing dropout on LoRA factors with test-time ensembling)
methods.paper_title: LoRA Dropout as a Sparsity Regularizer for Overfitting Control
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,\hat B\hat A,\quad \hat A = A\,\mathrm{diag}(m_A),\ \hat B = \mathrm{diag}(m_B)\,B,\quad m_A\in\{0,1\}^{d_{in}},\ m_B\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}}\sim\mathrm{Bern}(1-p);\quad \text{test time: } \bar o(x)=\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathcal{M}\big(x;\,W_0+s\hat B^{(n)}\hat A^{(n)}\big)
methods.locus: same as LoRA; also applied to AdaLoRA's P, Q factors
methods.structure: Bernoulli masks on the input columns of A and output rows of B (not on the rank dimension), so each entry of the product is zeroed with probability 2p-p^2; analysed as sparsity-regularized empirical risk minimization with a stability-based generalization bound, plus a Monte-Carlo test-time ensemble.
methods.mergeable_reason: Without test-time ensembling the trained BA merges like LoRA; the proposed test-time ensemble needs several stochastic forward passes and cannot be folded into a single weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0).
methods.key_idea: Even with few trainable parameters LoRA overfits; randomly dropping input/output coordinates of the LoRA factors acts as a sparsity regularizer that trades empirical risk against adaptation complexity, and averaging over dropout masks at test time tightens the bound further.
methods.results_note: Improves accuracy and calibration over LoRA/AdaLoRA on GLUE and SQuAD (DeBERTaV3-base) and on Alpaca instruction tuning of LLaMA2-7B in the paper's experiments.

relations.note: regularizer on the LoRA factors
the paper also applies the masks to AdaLoRA
both are regularizers for LoRA generalization (noise on factors vs. noise in full weight space)

methods.name: AsyLoRA
methods.full_name: Asymmetric LoRA (random frozen A, train only B)
methods.paper_title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,B\,Q,\quad Q\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random with orthonormal rows (Haar/Stiefel), frozen};\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained from } B=0
methods.locus: same as LoRA (RoBERTa, BART, LLaMA-2, ViT experiments)
methods.structure: Linear (not bilinear) parametrization: \Delta W ranges over \mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\otimes\mathrm{row}(Q) for a fixed random r-dim input subspace; freezing A gives least-squares/logistic regression on randomly projected features Qx, whereas freezing B only fits outputs projected onto a random subspace.
methods.mergeable_reason: B Q is an ordinary additive low-rank update that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 with Q random orthogonal and never updated.
methods.key_idea: A and B play asymmetric roles: A extracts input features (and a random A works about as well as a learned one) while B maps them to the task; training only B halves parameters, tightens information-theoretic generalization bounds, and lets one double r at fixed budget.
methods.results_note: Across RoBERTa, BART-Large, LLaMA-2 and ViT, B-only tuning with a random orthogonal A matches or beats standard LoRA at matched parameter count and improves out-of-domain accuracy on DomainBed.

relations.note: LoRA with eta_A = 0 and orthogonal random A
same freeze-A design, LoRA-FA motivated by activation memory
both rely on frozen random projections

methods.name: LoRA-GA
methods.full_name: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
methods.paper_title: LoRA-GA: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
methods.formula_latex: G=\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W_0)=USV^{\top}:\quad A_{\text{init}}=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\gamma}V_{[1:r]}^{\top},\ \ B_{\text{init}}=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\gamma}U_{[r+1:2r]},\ \ W_{\text{init}}=W_0-\eta\,B_{\text{init}}A_{\text{init}},\ \ \eta=\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r}};\qquad W=W_{\text{init}}+\eta\,BA
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Gradient-aligned initialization: (A_{init},B_{init}) minimize \|\eta^2 G A^{\top}A+\eta^2 BB^{\top}G-\zeta G\|_F, so the first LoRA step reproduces a scaled full-gradient step restricted to the top-2r singular directions of a sampled-batch gradient; rsLoRA-style \alpha/\sqrt{r} scaling and a d_{out}^{1/4}/\gamma factor give rank- and scale-stability.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_init + eta B A is a dense matrix; to ship a detachable adapter relative to the original W_0 the update is converted to eta(BA - B_init A_init) (rank <= 2r), which HF PEFT supports via path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion.
methods.identity_at_init: B_init A_init is non-zero, but it is subtracted from the base weight (W_init = W_0 - eta B_init A_init), so the network function is unchanged at step 0; requires a gradient-estimation pass over a few batches before training.
methods.key_idea: LoRA converges slowly because its random/zero initialization ignores the task; initializing A and B from the SVD of a (batch-estimated) full fine-tuning gradient makes the first LoRA updates mimic full fine-tuning, giving much faster convergence.
methods.results_note: Beats LoRA by 5.69% on a GLUE subset (T5-Base) and by 0.34 on MT-Bench, 11.52% on GSM8K and 5.05% on HumanEval (Llama 2-7B), with 2-4x faster convergence.

relations.note: uses alpha/sqrt(r) scaling for rank stability
both replace LoRA's zero/random init by an SVD-based init that compensates the base weight (PiSSA uses SVD of W_0, LoRA-GA of the gradient)
LoRA-One argues the top-r (not r+1..2r) singular subspace of the negative gradient is the correct alignment target

methods.name: LoRA-One
methods.full_name: LoRA-One (one-step full-gradient spectral initialization)
methods.paper_title: LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models, Provably and Efficiently
methods.formula_latex: USV^{\top}=\mathrm{SVD}\big(-\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W_0)\big),\ S\leftarrow S/S_{11}:\quad B_0=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{s}}\,U_{[:,1:r]}S_{[1:r]}^{1/2},\ \ A_0=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{s}}\,S_{[1:r]}^{1/2}V_{[:,1:r]}^{\top}\ \Rightarrow\ sB_0A_0=\big[-\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W_0)\big]_r/\sigma_1;\qquad W=W_0+sBA
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Spectral initialization of both factors from the best rank-r approximation of the (normalized) negative one-step full gradient, after which plain (or r\times r-preconditioned, 'LoRA-One-P') gradient descent is run; theory shows GD-trained adapters align with exactly these singular subspaces, so the init reaches the alignment immediately.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter is a standard additive rank-r product (initialized non-zero but still merged as W_0 + s B A).
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity-preserving: the base weight is not compensated, so the model starts at W_0 plus a normalized rank-r one-step full-gradient update (effectively a first spectral GD step).
methods.key_idea: Under gradient descent LoRA factors provably align with the top singular subspaces of the one-step full fine-tuning gradient; initializing there directly gives linear convergence (with preconditioning removing ill-conditioning) and corrects the subspace chosen by LoRA-GA.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA and LoRA-GA (and other variants) on GLUE (T5-base), GSM8K/MMLU/HumanEval fine-tuning of LLaMA-2-7B, e.g. +2.52 points over LoRA on GSM8K with few-shot CoT.

relations.note: both gradient-SVD initializations; LoRA-One uses the top-r subspace for both factors and no base-weight subtraction
LoRA-One-P uses the Zhang & Pilanci preconditioned AdamW
changes only the initialization (and optionally the optimizer)

methods.name: LoRA Without Regret
methods.full_name: LoRA Without Regret (Thinking Machines Lab recipe and analysis)
methods.paper_title: LoRA Without Regret
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(lora_alpha=32, target_modules='all-linear')  # same-LR AdamW, LR ~10x the FullFT LR
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA,\ \ \alpha=32,\ \ A_{ij}\sim\mathcal{U}\big(\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{d_{in}}}\big),\ B=0,\ \ \eta_A=\eta_B=\eta_{\text{LoRA}}\approx 10\,\eta_{\text{FullFT}};\ \ \text{apply to all linear layers incl. MLP/MoE}
methods.locus: all weight matrices, especially MLP and MoE layers (attention-only LoRA underperforms MLP-only LoRA)
methods.structure: Standard LoRA parametrization; of the four hyperparameters (\alpha, \eta_A, \eta_B, init scale of A) only two affect the dynamics, and with the 1/r multiplier and B=0 the expected first update \tfrac{1}{r}\sum_i b_ia_i^{\top} is rank-independent, making the optimal LR approximately independent of r.
methods.mergeable_reason: It is plain LoRA, so the adapter merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 with A uniform of scale 1/sqrt(d_in) (the PEFT default parametrization).
methods.key_idea: LoRA matches full fine-tuning in the regime that matters for post-training when applied to all layers (especially MLPs) with ~10x the FullFT learning rate and when the dataset does not exceed adapter capacity; RL needs very little capacity, so even rank-1 LoRA matches FullFT for policy-gradient training.
methods.results_note: On Llama 3 / Qwen3 models with Tulu3 and OpenThoughts3 SFT, LoRA matches FullFT until capacity is exceeded; on MATH/GSM8K/DeepMath RL even rank-1 LoRA matches FullFT; LoRA is less tolerant of large batch sizes; LoRA costs slightly more than 2/3 of FullFT FLOPs per pass.

relations.note: empirical study and recipe for vanilla LoRA
argues the default 1/r scaling already makes the optimal LR roughly rank-invariant
uses a single LR for A and B and shows two of the four hyperparameters are redundant

methods.name: Flat-LoRA
methods.full_name: Flat-LoRA (low-rank adaptation over a flat full-space loss landscape)
methods.paper_title: Flat-LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation over a Flat Loss Landscape
methods.formula_latex: \min_{A,B}\ \mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon_W}\,\mathcal{L}\big(W'+\varepsilon_W\big),\quad W'=W_0+sBA,\quad (\varepsilon_W)_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}\!\big(0,\tfrac{\sigma^2}{d_{in}}\|W'_{i,:}\|_2^2\big)\ \ (\text{fresh noise each step, regenerated from a seed})
methods.locus: same as LoRA (LLMs and text-to-image diffusion models)
methods.structure: Random-weight-perturbation (Bayesian expected loss) regularizer applied in the full d_{out}\times d_{in} weight space rather than in the (A,B) space, with filter(row)-norm-scaled Gaussian noise; a cheap relaxation of SAM's min-max over full-space perturbations.
methods.mergeable_reason: Noise is used only during training; the learned BA merges like LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0); the perturbation is zero-mean training noise only.
methods.key_idea: A minimum that is flat in LoRA's (A,B) coordinates can still be sharp in the full weight space; averaging the loss over full-space random weight perturbations steers LoRA toward full-space flat minima without SAM's extra gradient step or weight copy.
methods.results_note: Improves in-domain and out-of-domain generalization over LoRA on mathematical reasoning, coding, dialogue, instruction following and text-to-image generation in the paper's experiments.

relations.note: regularized LoRA training objective
alternative regularizer for LoRA generalization

methods.name: AltLoRA
methods.full_name: Alternating-projection LoRA
methods.paper_title: AltLoRA: Towards Better Gradient Approximation in Low-Rank Adaptation with Alternating Projections
methods.formula_latex: \text{even } t:\ A\leftarrow A-\eta\,\tfrac{1}{s^2}(B^{\top}B)^{-1}\nabla_A\mathcal{L}\ \ (\delta W=-\eta P_BG);\qquad \text{odd } t:\ B\leftarrow B-\eta\,\tfrac{1}{s^2}\nabla_B\mathcal{L}\,(AA^{\top})^{-1}\ \ (\delta W=-\eta\, G P_A);\quad \tilde M^B = M^BA_tA_{t+1}^{\top}(A_{t+1}A_{t+1}^{\top})^{-1}
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Alternating one-sided projections of the full gradient onto col(B) and row(A) (each the exact least-squares solution for the factor being updated), with momentum transported into the new low-rank subspace by an r\times r change-of-basis; avoids LoRA-Pro's non-unique X and full-size optimizer state.
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only change; the result is a standard LoRA adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization; Gram inverses are damped as (B^T B + lambda I)^{-1} to stay invertible when a factor is rank-deficient.
methods.key_idea: Instead of jointly matching the full gradient (LoRA-Pro), alternately update A and B so each step is an exact projection of the full gradient, and keep momentum aligned with the changing subspace without extra memory; this gives stable feature learning and transformation invariance.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA and its variants (including LoRA-Pro) across SFT and NLU tasks while keeping LoRA-level memory, narrowing the gap to full fine-tuning.

relations.note: same gradient-approximation goal, alternating instead of joint update, low-rank momentum
each half-step uses the same (B^T B)^{-1} / (AA^T)^{-1} preconditioners
concurrent alternating-update optimizer

methods.name: LoFT
methods.full_name: Low-rank adaptation that mimics Full fine-Tuning
methods.paper_title: LoFT: Low-Rank Adaptation That Behaves Like Full Fine-Tuning
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Six building blocks (alternating updates, scaled gradients, momentum recalibration across changing subspaces via C_k=(V_{k-1}^{\top}V_k)(V_k^{\top}V_k)^{-1}, second-moment alignment with cross terms, projected full update, gradient clipping) that make the low-rank step the tightest approximation to the AdamW full-fine-tuning step; reduces exactly to AdamW when r=\max(d_{in},d_{out}).
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only change; the adapter is a standard mergeable low-rank product.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits LoRA's zero-product initialization; Gram inverses fall back to pseudo-inverses when a factor is rank-deficient.
methods.key_idea: Not only gradients but also Adam's first and second moments are misaligned between LoRA and full fine-tuning; projecting and recalibrating them in the evolving low-rank subspace makes LoRA behave like full fine-tuning and removes the need to tune alpha.
methods.results_note: Substantially narrows the gap to full fine-tuning and consistently outperforms standard LoRA-style methods without increasing inference cost; memory overhead O((d_in+d_out) r^2) for second-moment calibration.

relations.note: concurrent alternating-update optimizers
Building Block 2 (scaled gradients) coincides with the Riemannian preconditioner
both align low-rank updates with full fine-tuning; LoFT also aligns optimizer states

methods.name: PoLAR
methods.full_name: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
methods.paper_title: PoLAR: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + X\Theta Y^{\top},\quad X\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r),\ Y\in\mathrm{St}(d_{in},r),\ \Theta\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r};\ \ X,Y\ \text{optimized on Stiefel manifolds (landing field)},\ \Theta\ \text{unconstrained}
methods.locus: same as LoRA (models from 350M to 27B)
methods.structure: Rank-r update written in polar/SVD-like form: two direction factors with orthonormal columns (points of Stiefel manifolds) and a free r\times r 'scale' core; the orthogonality constraint raises the stable rank of \Delta W and is maintained by retraction-free Riemannian (landing) optimization.
methods.mergeable_reason: X Theta Y^T is an ordinary rank-r matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Theta = 0 with X, Y drawn uniformly from the Stiefel manifolds, so Delta W = 0.
methods.key_idea: LoRA updates have very low stable rank (often near 1), wasting the allocated rank; constraining the two direction factors to be orthonormal and learning a free core, optimized with Riemannian methods, diversifies update directions and provably converges exponentially faster on a canonical problem.
methods.results_note: Consistent gains over LoRA on general language understanding, commonsense reasoning and mathematical reasoning benchmarks with base models from 350M to 27B parameters.

relations.note: uses Riemannian optimization for the adapter factors
both are direction-magnitude decompositions; PoLAR enforces orthogonality instead of column normalization
both use an SVD-like P Lambda Q style factorization of the update

papers.title: Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes
papers.claim: Training in a random low-dimensional affine subspace of parameter space reveals an 'intrinsic dimension' at which solutions appear, which is often far smaller than the parameter count and nearly constant across model sizes.
papers.relevance: Original evidence that useful updates live in tiny subspaces; LoRA's rank-r factorization is a structured, learnable version of the random-subspace construction.

papers.title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Pretrained LMs have very low fine-tuning intrinsic dimension (e.g. 200 random-projected parameters reach 90% of full RoBERTa performance on MRPC), pre-training lowers it, and larger models have lower intrinsic dimension; this yields parameter-count-free generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: The empirical and theoretical premise behind LoRA's low-rank hypothesis and behind treating PEFT as a choice of low-dimensional reparametrization.

papers.title: A Kernel-Based View of Language Model Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Prompt-based fine-tuning of pretrained LMs often exhibits kernel (eNTK) dynamics; in that regime, a Johnson-Lindenstrauss argument shows SGD-LoRA preserves the fine-tuning kernel, explaining why low-rank subspace methods work.
papers.relevance: Gives the linearized (functorial-in-the-tangent-space) picture in which LoRA is a random projection of the full fine-tuning kernel; baseline for NTK-regime LoRA theory.

papers.title: The Expressive Power of Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.claim: For fully connected networks LoRA can adapt any model to exactly represent any smaller target model once the LoRA rank exceeds (width of f) x (depth of target)/(depth of f), with quantified approximation error below that threshold; for Transformer networks rank-(embedding size/2) LoRA adapters suffice to adapt any model to a same-size target.
papers.relevance: Characterizes the image of the LoRA parametrization map, i.e. which fine-tuned functions are reachable at a given rank.

papers.title: LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima
papers.claim: In the NTK regime with N data points, full fine-tuning admits a low-rank solution of rank about sqrt(N); LoRA with rank of order sqrt(N) has no spurious local minima, so (S)GD finds such low-rank solutions, which generalize well.
papers.relevance: Landscape result for the bilinear LoRA parametrization; justifies optimizer-agnostic success of LoRA in the linearized regime.

papers.title: The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics
papers.claim: The two zero-product initializations (B=0, A random vs A=0, B random) are not equivalent: B=0 with random A allows larger stable learning rates and yields better fine-tuning on average.
papers.relevance: Shows that the symmetric-looking choices of which factor is zero break the A/B symmetry dynamically; complements LoRA+ and asymmetry results.

papers.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
papers.claim: On code and math (instruction tuning and continued pretraining) LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning at standard ranks but better preserves out-of-domain abilities; full fine-tuning learns perturbations of 10-100x higher rank than typical LoRA configs.
papers.relevance: Quantifies the capacity/forgetting trade-off that motivates high-rank-through-low-rank methods (ReLoRA, COLA, Delta-LoRA) and regularization views of LoRA.

papers.title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
papers.claim: LoRA and full fine-tuning produce spectrally different weights: LoRA introduces high-ranking 'intruder dimensions' (new singular vectors) that causally drive forgetting, and scaling them down recovers pre-training behaviour with little task loss.
papers.relevance: Shows that equal task accuracy does not mean equal morphisms in weight space; HF PEFT implements the mitigation as peft.tuners.lora.intruders.reduce_intruder_dimension.

papers.title: LoRA Training Provably Converges to a Low-Rank Global Minimum or It Fails Loudly (But it Probably Won't Fail)
papers.claim: Beyond linearization, in a 'generic regime' LoRA training converges either to a low-rank, small-magnitude global minimizer or to a qualitatively distinct high-rank, large-magnitude solution; zero-initialization and weight decay bias training toward the former.
papers.relevance: Non-linearized landscape theory explaining why zero-product initialization (identity at init) is not just cosmetic but an implicit bias.

papers.title: Understanding the Learning Dynamics of LoRA: A Gradient Flow Perspective on Low-Rank Adaptation in Matrix Factorization
papers.claim: For LoRA on matrix factorization under gradient flow, small initialization converges to a neighbourhood of the optimum whose error is governed by misalignment between pretrained and target singular spaces; a small spectral initialization converges to arbitrary precision.
papers.relevance: Clean dynamical model connecting initialization scale and singular-subspace alignment, the mechanism exploited by LoRA-GA and LoRA-One.

papers.title: Learning Rate Matters: Vanilla LoRA May Suffice for LLM Fine-tuning
papers.claim: Re-evaluating nine LoRA variants (initialization, architectural and optimizer changes, incl. PiSSA, MiLoRA, LoRA-GA, DoRA, LoFT) with thorough hyperparameter search shows they prefer different learning-rate ranges but reach similar peak performance (within 1-2%) once LR is tuned; the LR differences track the largest Hessian eigenvalue.
papers.relevance: Important caution for any taxonomy: many training-dynamics variants may be reparametrizations of the learning rate rather than genuinely different adaptation morphisms.

papers.title: LoRA Meets Dropout under a Unified Framework
papers.claim: LoRA fine-tuning is still overfitting-prone; transformer dropout variants (DropKey, DropAttention, HiddenCut) can be unified by dropping position, structural pattern and compensation, and the best combination (HiddenKey) improves LoRA on NLU and NLG.
papers.relevance: Complements LoRA Dropout: places regularization of the low-rank branch inside a general design space.

notes: Coverage: 20 method entries (LoRA, rsLoRA, LoRA+, LoRA-FA, Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA, LoRA-RITE, LoRA-Pro, ReLoRA, Delta-LoRA, COLA, PeriodicLoRA, LoRA Dropout, AsyLoRA, LoRA-GA, LoRA-One, LoRA Without Regret, Flat-LoRA, AltLoRA, LoFT, PoLAR) and 12 theory/analysis papers. All seeds confirmed and kept. UNIFYING OBSERVATION (useful for the categorical narrative): with G = grad_W L, P_B = B(B^T B)^{-1}B^T, P_A = A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A, the optimizer-geometry subfamily differs only in which projection of G onto the tangent space T_{BA} of the rank-r stratum it applies: LoRA-FA = G P_A (one side, A frozen); Riemannian scaled GD = P_B G + G P_A (double-counts P_B G P_A); LoRA-Pro = P_B G + (I-P_B) G P_A (exact orthogonal tangent projection; verified algebraically from its Theorem 2.1); AltLoRA/LoFT = alternate P_B G and G P_A; LoRA-RITE = adaptive (Adam-like) GL(r)-invariant version. Plain LoRA/LoRA+/rsLoRA are NOT GL(r)-gauge invariant; these are. Restart methods (ReLoRA, COLA, PeriodicLoRA, Delta-LoRA) instead escape the rank-r stratum by composing updates additively (sum of rank-r terms). HF PEFT status (checked against main and release notes, v0.21.1 on 2026-09-29): rsLoRA = LoraConfig(use_rslora=True); LoRA+ = create_loraplus_optimizer; LoRA-FA optimizer since v0.16.0 (2025-07); LoRA-GA init since v0.19.0 (2026-04); Riemannian preconditioned optimizer since v0.21.0 (2026-09-15); PEFT also ships reduce_intruder_dimension from the Illusion-of-Equivalence paper. PEFT's lora_dropout is ordinary input dropout on x, NOT the LoRA Dropout method of Lin et al. (masks on A columns / B rows + test-time ensemble). Caveats: (1) LoRA-FA: v1 (2023) only froze A; the gradient projection (AA^T)^{-1} appears in the current arXiv version and in PEFT; the arXiv listing metadata now shows the title 'LoRA-FA: Efficient and Effective Low Rank Representation Fine-tuning' while the paper PDF/HTML keeps the original title used here. (2) PeriodicLoRA's momentum unloading is described only in words ('scale BA by (1-m) and A, B by m'); formula given as described, confidence medium. (3) PoLAR may also belong to an SVD-structured/reparametrization family; included here for its Riemannian-optimization angle (medium). (4) LoRA-GA and LoRA-One overlap with an initialization family (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, EVA, CorDA, LoRA-SB are deliberately excluded here). (5) Tension worth showing on the site: rsLoRA says scale must be alpha/sqrt(r) for large-rank stability, while LoRA Without Regret finds alpha/r makes the optimal LR roughly rank-independent (early-training argument); Lee et al. 2026 further find most variants equalize once LR is tuned. (6) Venues from OpenReview: LoRA-RITE ICLR 2025 Oral, LoRA-Pro ICLR 2025 Spotlight, LoFT ICLR 2026 Poster, AltLoRA NeurIPS 2025, Illusion of Equivalence NeurIPS 2025, LoRA-One ICML 2025 Oral; Delta-LoRA (ICLR 2024 submission), LoRA Dropout (withdrawn ICLR 2025 submission), COLA and PeriodicLoRA remain arXiv-only. Considered but excluded (low uptake or other family): DyLoRA (rank-allocation family), LoRA-the-Explorer/LTE (2402.16828, parallel merged LoRA heads for pre-training; ~18 citations, arXiv only), ALLoRA (2410.09692, ~3 citations), LoRA-SB (init family), LoRA-GA^2 (2608.19800) and 'One Rate Is Not Enough' (2609.05885) (Aug/Sep 2026, no uptake yet), GaLore/Flora (gradient-projection family), QLoRA (quantization family), HydraLoRA (MoE family), DoRA (decomposition family).
